label: Reconstructed Césairean Négritude as vitalist-decolonial creative humanity
description: Kisukidi reads Aimé Césaire alongside Bergsonian vitalism to show how Négritude invents an open, non-essentialist universalism from colonial rupture.
dialecticalTension: Revitalizes Négritude for contemporary Francophone African philosophy.
historicalContext: Paris VIII / Dialogue with Césaire and Bergson (2013–2020s).

label: Extended Congolese critique of colonial epistemology into aesthetic politics
description: Continuing Mudimbe’s interrogation of European universalism, Kisukidi explores how diasporic aesthetics and curatorial praxis contest Western epistemic monopoly.
dialecticalTension: Bridges Congolese archaeology of knowledge with contemporary political aesthetics.
